title: Part 1 Practice: Elements and Controls of Climate

questions.text: The MAIN difference between weather and climate is:
options: A) Weather is short-term, climate is long-term average
B) Weather is long-term, climate is short-term
C) They are the same thing
questions.correct_answer: A) Weather is short-term, climate is long-term average
questions.explanation: WEATHER is the SHORT-TERM atmospheric condition (hourly, daily changes). CLIMATE is the LONG-TERM average of weather over 30+ years. Weather can change in minutes; climate changes over decades.
Ethiopia lies between 3°N and 15°N LATITUDE — a TROPICAL location. This means Ethiopia receives DIRECT sunlight year-round, giving warm temperatures. Option C (33°E-48°E) is LONGITUDE.

questions.text: The Earth's axis is tilted at approximately:
questions.explanation: The Earth's axis is tilted at 23.5° from the vertical. This TILT causes the SEASONS as different parts of the Earth receive varying amounts of sunlight throughout the year.

options: A) Longest day of the year
B) Equal day and night worldwide
C) Shortest day of the year
questions.correct_answer: B) Equal day and night worldwide
questions.explanation: During an EQUINOX (March 21 and September 23), day and night are EQUAL (12 hours each) everywhere on Earth. The sun is directly OVERHEAD at the equator.

questions.text: Examine the diagram. What does the SUN's position at TROPIC OF CANCER indicate?

questions.explanation: When the sun is directly overhead at the TROPIC OF CANCER (23.5°N) on JUNE 21, it's the SUMMER SOLSTICE — the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere (including Ethiopia).

questions.text: Ethiopia's temperature DECREASES with altitude at approximately:
questions.explanation: The ENVIRONMENTAL (normal) lapse rate is about 6.5°C per 1,000 meters of altitude gain. This is why Ethiopia's HIGHLANDS are cooler than its LOWLANDS despite being near the equator.

questions.text: The DRY ADIABATIC lapse rate is:
questions.explanation: The DRY ADIABATIC lapse rate is 10°C per 1,000m — the rate at which RISING DRY air cools. It's FASTER than the wet adiabatic rate (5°C/km) because dry air doesn't release latent heat.

questions.text: Why is the WET ADIABATIC lapse rate SLOWER than the dry rate?
options: D) Water is colder than air
questions.explanation: When SATURATED (wet) air rises, condensation occurs, releasing LATENT HEAT. This heat partially COUNTERACTS the cooling, making the wet adiabatic rate (5°C/km) slower than the dry rate (10°C/km).

questions.text: Examine the lapse rate diagram. Which line is STEEPEST?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='150' viewBox='0 0 350 150'><rect width='350' height='150' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><line x1='30' y1='130' x2='330' y2='130' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='30' y1='10' x2='30' y2='130' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='30' y1='20' x2='330' y2='120' stroke='#14b8a6' stroke-width='3'/><text x='200' y='80' fill='#14b8a6' font-size='8' font-weight='bold'>A</text><line x1='30' y1='10' x2='330' y2='130' stroke='#f43f5e' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5,3'/><text x='250' y='110' fill='#f43f5e' font-size='8' font-weight='bold'>B</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Line B (red dashed) is STEEPEST — it has the FASTEST temperature decrease with altitude (10°C/km = DRY ADIABATIC). Line A (green) is gentler (6.5°C/km = ENVIRONMENTAL). Steeper = faster cooling.

questions.text: Why does Addis Ababa (2,400m) have moderate climate DESPITE being tropical?
options: A) It's far from the equator
B) High ALTITUDE cools the temperature
questions.correct_answer: B) High ALTITUDE cools the temperature
questions.explanation: Addis Ababa's HIGH ALTITUDE (2,400m) COOLS its temperature despite its tropical location. At 2,400m, temperature is about 15.6°C cooler than sea level (6.5°C/km × 2.4km). This is why Ethiopian highlands have pleasant climate.
